newsitem.title: USA: Four junk deals to hit US corporate bond mkt. [CORRECTED 18:40 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Four junk deals to hit US corporate bond mkt. [CORRECTED 18:40 GMT]

text.p: Four new high-yield bond offerings were expected to hit the U.S. corporate bond market by the end of the week as issuers rushed to tap strong demand for new paper from junk investors, syndicate officials said.
Adelphia Communications Corp, a Coudersport, Penn.-based cable company, is speedily putting together a 144a offering of at least $200 million in senior notes via Smith Barney Inc.
The company said it will use the proceeds from the offering to redeem a portion of its 12-1/2 percent notes which become callable in May, as well as to pay down bank debt.
"This is a very savvy move," said one analyst. "The company is basically taking advantage of a very hot market to manage their balance sheet and increase liquidity for refinancing."

The deal, which is expected to price on Friday, may be increased to as much as $400 million if buyside demand is strong enough, market players said. Adelphia has a total of $400 million of 12-1/2 percent bonds outstanding.
Price talk on the current offering is 9-7/8 percent to 10 percent, they said.
Other junk deals expected to price by the end of the week include:

-a $175 million 144a offering of zero coupon bonds from Diamond Cable Communications, a British cable company. Goldman Sachs & Co is the underwriter for the deal, which is expected to price on Thursday.
-a $125 million 144a offering of senior subordinated notes from GFSI Inc, a specialty apparel manufacturer, via Donaldson Lufkin & Jenrette Securities Corp for Thursday.
-a $125 million 144a offering of senior subordinated notes from Packard Industries Inc via Merrill Lynch & Co.
The deal, expected to price on Friday, was upsized from $100 million due to strong investor demand. Price talk is 9-3/8 percent to 9-5/8 percent, market sources said.
Activity in the high-grade corporate bond market was also picking up on Thursday, syndicate officials said.
J.C. Penny & Co Inc is expected to place $400 million in debt via Credit Suisse First Boston, syndicate sources said on Thursday.
Goldman Sachs is leading a $100 million offering of five-year debt for Macsaver Financial Services, syndicate sources said.
And Harnischfeger Industries Inc, a manufacturer of industrial equipment, plans to sell $100 million in bonds via Lehman Brothers Inc and Merrill Lynch, market players said.
On Friday, Ford Motor Credit is expected to price $1 billion in five-year notes in a global offering via Goldman Sachs & Salomon Brothers Inc.
Price talk on the deal is 38-39 basis points over comparable Treasuries.
(Corrects to show Ford Motor Credit deal, set for Friday, had not yet been priced).
Also on Thursday morning, Sakura Bank sold $1 billion in subordinated perpetual step-up debt in a 144a Eurobond offering via Merrill Lynch.
The deal consisted of a $400 million tranche with a fixed-rate coupon for five-years and a $600 milllion tranche with a floating-rate coupon.
